messages:
maria: Heads up — seeing a persistent I/O saturation pattern on /dev/nvme0 across ~18 hosts in us-west1. GPU attach latency up, attach_wait alerts firing. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/kvqIOps/host-iops?orgId=1&var-region=us-west1 :eyes:

alex: yep saw the attach_waits around 02:10-02:40 UTC, tail latencies spiked to ~200-300ms. IOPS fine but queue_wait climbed. :+1:

jin: likely the janitor scrub cadence. last deploy bumped scrub_concurrency in v2.4.1 to 8 to speed cleanup; that can hammer small devices during scaleups. config lives at /etc/janitor/config.yaml on provisioners.

maria: ah that aligns — timestamps match the scrub window. can we throttle quickly?

jin: quick mitigation I pushed to the daemonset: set scrub_concurrency=2 and lower scrub_window parallelism. command I ran on a node to test:

```
sudo sed -i 's/scrub_concurrency: 8/scrub_concurrency: 2/' /etc/janitor/config.yaml
sudo systemctl restart janitor
```

jin: after that host-level queue_wait dropped ~70% on the canary node.

sam: another fast stopgap: prevent new GPU attaches to the worst nodes for 15m while we stabilize. e.g.

```
kubectl label node ip-10-0-40-12.us-west1.internal node.kubernetes.io/attach-backoff=true --overwrite
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-40-12.us-west1.internal   # avoid new pods
```

sam: also lowered kernel queue depth on the test node to reduce burst pressure: `echo 64 > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/nr_requests` (monitor first).

maria: applied janitor change cluster-wide and cordoned the top 10 affected nodes. after 10m overall attach_wait alerts dropped and median attach latency went from 120ms -> 30ms. thanks.

maria: followups: 1) revert scrub_concurrency bump in next release, 2) add a temporary auto-throttle for janitor when attach_wait > 100ms, 3) add a routed fallback for GPU requests to prefer nodes with < 30% queue_wait in Optimize recommendations.

ops-bot: [alert] attach_wait.us-west1 resolved (was firing on 18 hosts). Automated note: incident window 02:10-02:36 UTC.

alex: logging a retro item - cost/latency tradeoff from increasing janitor parallelism. might be worth an opt-in aggressive-mode for low-cost clusters only.

maria: agreed — filing a follow-up ticket and plan to run a canary across apac/us regions before any future concurrency increases. :memo:
